items.title: Georg Brunis Interview, 1958-06-03
items.q: I was playing the upright alto and he was playing the trombone. So he got under the weather one time and he didn't show up. And, uh, we were playing down at Crescent City Carnival Club.

ctx.x: Well, how did you learn to play so wonderfully? I mean, you not only have a wonderful ear and wonderful tone, but even your position. I mean, you got around...

Well, Pansy Lane, that's Papa Lane's son. His name is Alfred. They called him Pansy. He played the trumpet and his brother-in-law, Leon Smello. I was playing the upright alto and he was playing the trombone. So he got under the weather one time and he didn't show up. And, uh, we were playing down at Crescent City Carnival Club. And, uh, Pansy says, uh, geez, what are we going to do for a trombone? He says, I said, well, I can play the trombone parts on the alto. He says, why don't you try the trombone, Bruno? So…
